result.question: Why can a higher-power processor still be more energy-efficient for a particular task?
result.answer: A processor that consumes more power can still be more energy-efficient if it completes the task significantly faster.

retrieved_chunks.text: ENERGY AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY A processor that consumes more power can still be more energy-efficient if it completes the task significantly faster.

ENERGY AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY The key idea is that power and energy are not the same thing, and when comparing processors for a particular task, energy is usually the better metric. ENERGY EFFICIENCY STRATEGIES • 2. Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) is the adjustment of power and speed settings on a computing device's various processors, controller chips and peripheral devices to optimize resource allotment for tasks and maximize power saving when those resources are not needed. • If the current task is computationally intensive, meaning it requires the processor to consume more energy and run at a higher frequency, DVFS will ensure that the voltage and frequency increase to match the requirements. However,if the processor needs to run a low-priority or less computationally intensive task where high speed and throughput are not required,it will adjust accordingly.

LATENCY AND BANDWIDTH • Bandwidth = the amount of data that can be transferred per unit of time. • Bandwidth tells us "How much data can I transfer per second?“ • It is usually measured in: MB/s GB/s • Higher bandwidth = more data can be transferred per second.

ENERGY EFFICIENCY STRATEGIES • Overclocking. • Intel started offering T urbomode in 2008, where the chip decides that it is safe to run at a higher clock rate for a short time, possibly on just a few cores, until temperature starts to rise. For example, the 3.3 GHz Core i7 can run in short bursts for 3.6 GHz. Indeed, the highest-performing microprocessors each year since 2008 have all offered temporary overclocking of about 10% over the nominal clock rate. • For single-threaded code, these microprocessors can turn off all cores but one and run it faster. Note that, although the operating system can turn off T urbomode, there is no notification once it is enabled, so the programmers may be surprised to see their programs vary in performance because of room temperature.
